thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: CUDA OOM on node gpu-12a while serving model=redwood/x-large-v2. headroom reported: 2.5GB, allocation failed requesting 7.9GB. 3 replicas impacted in eu-west-1. Auto-restart triggered on 2 containers. Paging flagged.

alex: Ack. I'm on call. tagging infra-sre and eng-runtime. Can someone grab the last 5m of allocator logs and KV cache stats?

priya: grabbing logs now. attaching tail here.
priya: ```
[2026-03-15T10:03:12Z] allocator: total_free=3.1GB largest_free_block=1.2GB headroom_reserved=2.5GB
[2026-03-15T10:03:13Z] kv_cache: pinned_blocks=128 pinned_bytes=4.6GB
[2026-03-15T10:03:13Z] runtime: serve_request(id=xyz) try_alloc(7.9GB) -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-15T10:03:14Z] allocator: attempt_reserve_reclaim -> success? false
```

sam: that largest_free_block=1.2GB is the smoking gun. fragmentation + pinned KV blocks means even though headroom shows ~2.5GB, we don't have a contiguous block for a big allocation.

infra-sre: confirming node-level metrics: gpu-12a shows 94% utilization on GPU memory, but system free reports ~3GB due to many small holes. Paging to host is enabled but we prefer not to hit host too often.

alex: what's current reserve policy for this node? any global sparepool?

priya: reserve_policy: dynamic with sparepool=6GB, headroom_pct=10%. But sparepool is fragmented; there are reserved blocks pinned by active KV caches and the allocator's slab alignment.

sam: immediate mitigation ideas (short-term, live):
- reduce batch_size for x-large to 4 -> fewer simultaneous large allocations
- disable kv_cache for the model variant to free pinned blocks
- force a soft-evict of sparepool to consolidate free blocks (toggle reserve_reclaim)
- if needed, cordon+drain node and let pods reschedule to other GPUs

alex: do we have a runtime flag to disable KV cache per-model without redeploy?

priya: yes, we can flip feature flag via console or "redwoodctl models update --model x-large-v2 --kv-cache=false". It'll take ~15s to roll.

alex: can someone run that now and reduce batch size? also mark customers impacted.

maria: reducing batch size on the route: ```redwoodctl route update --route /v1/generate --model x-large-v2 --max-batch-size 4``` applying... :hourglass:

priya: flipping kv cache off for x-large-v2 now: ```redwoodctl models update --name x-large-v2 --kv_cache=off --rollout=canary:1``` response: accepted.

support-bot: Customer impact: 3 customers in eu-west-1 showing 500s from the last 10m. Error rate ~1.8% -> 2.4 errors/min. One large enterprise (acct=redwood-fin) reporting degraded throughput. Notified CSM.

infra-sre: soft-evict attempt: we're toggling allocator.reserve_reclaim=1 on gpu-12a to trigger consolidation. Command: ```ssh gpu-12a -- sudo systemctl set-environment ALLOCATOR_FORCE_RECLAIM=1 && sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime``` Doing a rolling restart of runtime on that node. Be aware this may drop in-flight requests.

sam: alternate lighter option: trigger per-pod local gc: `curl -X POST http://pod-ip:8600/debug/allocator/reclaim` — that'll try to free pinned cache segments first. Might be less disruptive.

alex: go for the per-pod reclaim on the 3 affected pods first. Priya/infra-sre coordinate. If that doesn't work in 2 minutes, proceed with disable-kv and batch reduction.

priya: issuing per-pod reclaim to pod gpu-12a-pod-1/2/3 now. responses: pod-1 -> reclaimed 1.6GB, pod-2 -> reclaimed 0.9GB, pod-3 -> reclaimed 1.4GB.

sam: good, that increases largest_free_block to ~2.8GB. We're seeing fewer allocation failures. Dropping error rate in metrics.

support-bot: error rate fell to 0.6% in the last 3m. Customer requests still showing some spikes but throughput recovering.

alex: status check: are we green to keep these changes (kv_cache off, batch_size 4) as a short-term mitigation? We need a plan to avoid recurrence.

priya: kv_cache is currently in canary=1; only a single replica has it off. We should promote across the fleet in eu-west-1 for x-large-v2 until we have a fix. I'll rollout to 50% now then 100% if stable.

sam: longer term engineering actions:
- allocator: implement compaction hinting to coalesce small free blocks into larger contiguous regions (INF-2345)
- reserved blocks: change alignment to smaller granularity for large-model allocations or implement split/merge of reserved blocks
- KV cache: opportunistic eviction for large single-alloc requests (policy change)
- observability: add metric `largest_free_block_bytes` per-GPU and an alert when largest_free_block < X% of headroom

infra-sre: short term ops tasks: collect full allocator dump from gpu-12a, snapshot /var/log/redwood/allocator*.log and upload to S3 bucket s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2049991111/

priya: starting dump now. command: ```sudo redwood-allocator dump --out /tmp/alloc-dump.gz && aws s3 cp /tmp/alloc-dump.gz s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2049991111/``` ETA ~30s.

alex: good. Maria, keep an eye on customer comms. Sam & Priya, please schedule a post-incident triage tomorrow and link INF-2345. I'll file the incident ticket now.

maria: customers notified with mitigation note. CSMs updated. No escalations yet. :white_check_mark:

sam: note for postmortem: fragmentation risk increases after long-running node with many cache churns + large model allocations. Recommend a weekly compaction window or auto-drain to re-pack allocations.

priya: dump uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/2049991111/alloc-dump.gz

infra-sre: node gpu-12a is stable with new settings, error rate down to 0.2%. We'll keep node online but monitoring for 2 hours.

alex: summary for the thread:
- root cause: allocator fragmentation + pinned KV cache blocks prevented contiguous large allocation -> CUDA OOM despite headroom metric being nonzero.
- immediate mitigations: per-pod reclaim, temporary KV cache disable for model, lowered batch_size, reserve_reclaim toggle.
- customer impact: brief degraded throughput for 3 customers in eu-west-1, no data loss.
- follow-ups: INF-2345 (allocator compaction + metrics), collect more dumps, add alert on largest_free_block_bytes, evaluate permanent KV eviction policy.

support-bot: Incident ticket created: INCIDENT-2049991111 (linked to INF-2345). Assigned: sam, priya.

alex: closing on-call thread for now. If anything spikes, re-open. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident state -> MONITORING.
